summary: Sustained 5xx increase from mixed embeddings + streaming workload causing runtime worker starvation and TLS socket leakage
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme AI) reported sustained 5xx rate increase on production routing for a mixed workload that runs concurrent embeddings uploads and long-lived streaming chat sessions. Errors started ~2026-03-13T07:00Z and persisted for ~2h until mitigation.

Impact:
- ~18% error rate on the customer's API calls for 90 minutes; several timeouts and connection resets seen in embedding upload paths and streaming sessions.
- Customer observed partial failures in long-prompt generation and truncated embedding batches.

Environment:
- Hosted API (prod) serving enterprise tenant on us-west-2, route pinned to open-chat-mix-v2 with embedded-uploads fallback to embed-tiny-v1.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start 50 concurrent streaming chat sessions with long-context prompts (~8k tokens).
2) Simultaneously POST 200 small embedding batches (size 128) using the bulk upload endpoint from the same tenant.
3) Observe elevated 5xx and slow first byte on both streaming and embedding endpoints within ~5-10 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- API Gateway returned 502/503/504 at varying rates. Runtime upstream logs show repeated "worker thread pool exhaustion" and "tls: too many open sockets" warnings.
- Heap and thread count on several runtimes climbed steadily; kernel-level socket table showed large number of TIME_WAIT sockets pinned by keepalive misconfiguration.

Initial mitigation applied:
- Support throttled customer to a conservative concurrency cap (20 streaming sessions, staggered embedding batches) at 2026-03-13T09:05Z which immediately reduced error rate to <1%.
- Applied temporary rate-limit override on the tenant to force connection pooling expiration to 30s to relieve socket buildup.
comments: Leah Torres (Support) 2026-03-13T08:45Z: Customer reports 18% 5xx across streaming and embedding endpoints. Provided logs and timeline. Escalating to SRE.
Mikhail Ivanov (SRE) 2026-03-13T08:55Z: Acknowledged. Beginning triage on us-west-2 runtimes and API gateway metrics (linking dashboards).
Customer (ACME Ops) 2026-03-13T09:02Z: We can throttle from our side but need a permanent fix; this is impacting nightly batch jobs. Provide ETA?

Mikhail Ivanov (SRE) 2026-03-13T09:10Z: We've applied a tenant-side concurrency cap and a temporary keepalive expiry. Error rate dropped. Investigating root cause; will follow up with plan and patch ETA.

Eng on-call (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-13T11:00Z: Identified a code path where embedding upload handlers create short-lived upstream TLS connections per shard upload and don't reuse HTTP/2 streams when mixed with streaming sessions. This amplifies fd usage and causes runtime worker queue stalls under mixed patterns.
Leah Torres (Support) 2026-03-13T12:05Z: Customer confirmed reduced errors after throttling. They've requested a postmortem and timeline for permanent remediation.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13T09:15Z — Grafana (api-gateway/error-rate) spike aligns with tenant concurrency ramp; per-route CPU and eventloop metrics show increased syscall wait times.
Kibana logs: /var/log/runtime/upstream.log lines show repeated 'worker-pool-saturated' and 'accept queue backlog > threshold' entries between 07:00Z and 09:00Z.
Packet captures and socket stats indicate large number of half-closed TLS sockets with keepalive timers not being reclaimed due to a race between stream cancellation and socket pool return.

Hypothesis: Mixed workload causes frequent creation of short-lived TLS client connections from embedding shard uploads which compete for runtime worker threads used by streaming session heartbeats. Under high concurrency this leads to worker starvation and apigw returns 502/504.

Confirmed with load test: replaying customer's pattern on staging reproduced increased fd pressure and worker queue latency; enabling HTTP/2 multiplexing on the embed path and reusing client connections eliminated the failure mode in test.

Related PR: runtime change to connection pooling and socket reuse https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5421 — adds an LRU-backed client connection reuse for embedding shard uploads and fixes cancellation->pool-return race.
Slack channel: #support (thread t12345) and #sre-alerts contain timestamps and links to traces.
resolution:
Workaround + permanent fix applied: 1) Temporary customer throttling and keepalive expiry reduced immediate impact (applied 2026-03-13T09:05Z). 2) Deployed runtime patch (PR #5421) to staging 2026-03-13T14:20Z and to production us-west-2 2026-03-14T02:45Z which enables HTTP/2 multiplexing on embed uploads and fixes socket pool return race. 3) Increased accept-queue tuning and added a safety throttle when fd usage exceeds threshold. Post-deploy, error rates returned to baseline (<0.5%) for Acme AI.

Follow-ups:
- ENG to backport fixes to dedicated/private images (INT-44220).
- Monitoring: add a composite alert for mixed-embed-stream fd pressure and worker-queue-latency.
- Runbook update: document tenant throttling knobs and recommended embed-upload client guidance for large customers.
- Customer success: scheduled call with Acme AI on 2026-03-16 to review changes and recommended client-side best practices.
